## Motivation & Overview

Benchmarking quantum simulators and hardware backends often suffers from opaque configuration drift, non-reproducible post-processing, and unverifiable execution claims. **GaugeBench** [@amaral2026gaugebench] provides an open benchmark harness that wraps two distinct physics engines:

- **QIC Engine (Gate-Based / IBM-compatible):** Circuits derived from the [Quasicrystal Inflation Code](quasicrystal-inflation-code.qmd) [@amaral2025qic] testing constrained Fibonacci-subspace state preparation and braid gate fidelity.
- **Hierarchy Engine (Quantum Annealing / D-Wave-compatible):** Constrained Ising/QUBO problem instances probing hierarchical frustration and energy landscapes.

Every benchmark execution emits a cryptographically verifiable **Content-Addressable Receipt (CAR)** recording input circuit/Hamiltonian hashes, backend parameters, raw measurement counts, and deterministic verification checks—executable reproducibly on free local simulators or cloud quantum hardware backends.
